Pianists in cutting contests often played in this fast style of playing where the left hand alternates bass notes and chord tones. This style was popularized by pianists like Fats Waller and Willie “The Lion” Smith.
This teacher of Fats Waller and rival of Willie “The Lion” Smith was called “The Father of Stride.” He composed “The Charleston” for the Broadway musical Runnin’ Wild.

bonuses.leadin: In this short story, the titular character ironically rebuffs a character’s “ermine toque” at the Jardins Publiques (“zhar-DAN poo-BLEEK”). For 10 points each:
parts: Name this story where the protagonist’s illusory connection with a public park is shattered when her fur is compared to a “fried whiting.”
“Miss Brill” appears in a collection titled for this other story, in which a sobbing Laura struggles to explain life after the title event resumes following Mr. Scott’s death.
This New Zealand-born author of “Miss Brill” and “The Garden Party” described her stories as a “cry against corruption” in a letter to her husband.

bonuses.leadin: Whitewater and blackwater flow without mixing near this city at the Meeting of Waters. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this city that lies near the confluence of the Amazon River and the Rio Negro. A pink opera house in this city features in the opening scene of Werner Herzog’s Fitzcarraldo.

Much of the Amazon’s whitewater comes from this Peruvian river which joins the Ucayali near Iquitos. A coastal Atlantic state with its capital at São Luis is named after this river because it used to be the name for the entire Amazon.
This mountain range is the source of the Amazonian whitewater rivers that produce great biodiversity when they flood varzéa forests. This mountain range contains Lake Titicaca.

bonuses.leadin: Although quiet standing seems static, the body actually rocks slightly in the sagittal plane in a way once attributed to action like these objects in the muscles. For ten points each:
parts: Several lower leg muscles store and release energy like what compressible coiled objects?
Quiet standing is often modeled as this system, by assigning one rotational degree of freedom to the ankle. The cartpole is also modeled as this system in control theory.

Ironically, the inverted pendulum that enables quiet standing lacks this property, which can be achieved through negative feedback. An equilibrium point has this property if the potential energy is locally minimized.

bonuses.leadin: This psychologist and Martin Buber discussed the relationship between their ideas at a 1957 dialogue. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this psychologist who pioneered student-centered learning. This psychologist developed a procedure that aims at the “actualizing tendency” of people through “unconditional positive regard.”

Buber’s I-Thou relationship inspired the relationship between the two participants in Rogers’ person-centered form of this practice. Stoicism inspired the cognitive behavioral type of this conversational mental health treatment.

In this book, Rogers uses Buber’s phrase “confirming the other” to describe how therapists should ideally interact with their clients. This 1961 Carl Rogers book is subtitled “A Therapist’s View of Psychotherapy.”

bonuses.leadin: A navigator from this island group named Anagumang legendarily ordered rocks to be cut into the shape of a full moon. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Micronesian island group, which uses a unique currency of large disk-like rai stones with circles in the center that were often quarried from neighboring Palau.
These objects are used as tabu currency by the Papua New Guinean Tolai people. People from West Africa and China harvested these objects from cowries.
Santa Cruz Islanders used these objects to fashion tevau money coils. High valuable cloaks were created by the Maori by plucking green ones of these objects from kakapo birds.

bonuses.leadin: Several Revolutionary War heroes have now been adopted as queer icons. For 10 points each:
parts: This Founding Father exchanged flirty letters with John Laurens, leading some historians to speculate he may have been bisexual. He would later become the first Secretary of the Treasury.

One of America’s earliest openly gay figures was this Continental Army general, who likely had a romantic relationship with his aide-de-camp William North. This general’s secretary John Mulligan was also gay.

The discipline of a retreat by Charles Lee at this battle is credited to Baron von Steuben’s training. Molly Pitcher legendarily loaded cannons after taking her husband’s place at this 1778 New Jersey battle.

bonuses.leadin: The 2015 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to an author raised in this non-Ukraine country whose works are described as “documentary novels.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this modern day country home to journalist Svetlana Alexievich, who interviewed over 200 women soldiers in War’s Unwomanly Face.
Alexievich is best known for a book titled Voices from this Ukrainian site, where a nuclear disaster occured in 1986.
Alexievich’s works were described by the Nobel Committee using this adjective. Mikhail Bakhtin coined this term to describe the multiplicity of voices in Dostoyevsky novels.

bonuses.leadin: Methods of how to pattern muqarnas and these objects are outlined in the Topkapı (“top-copy”) Scroll. For 10 points each:
parts: Name these objects, some of which are fawn-colored in Haft Rang designs. Girih examples of these objects decorate the vaults and ceilings of many Iranian mosques.
The quasicrystal patterns of Girih tiling are greatly based on the right-angled styling of the Kufic form of this elaborate writing artform.

Many Girih patterns documented in the Topkapı Scroll are based on strapwork found in this city’s Darb-e Imam shrine. The courtyard of this city’s Friday Mosque is flanked by four iwans decorated with turquoise tiling.

bonuses.leadin: In this film, Boaz relates how he is deeply disturbed by a recurrent nightmare of killing 26 rabid dogs in a village to his friend, director Ari Folman. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this animated film titled for a sequence in which a character dances with a machine gun while a piece by Chopin plays in the background.

Waltz with Bashir was just the second animated film nominated for the Best Foreign Language; the first was a film mostly set in this country. A Separation and The Salesman are Oscar-winning films from this country, the setting of Close-Up.
Persepolis was beaten for the 2007 Animated Picture Oscar by this pioneering 3D animation studio, who has dominated the category with films like Wall-E and Up.

bonuses.leadin: Nancy Knowlton et al. studied this process by comparing the morphologies of snapping shrimp populations living on opposite sides of the isthmus of Panama. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this process in which genetic incompatibility is propagated by dispersal and vicariance. During this process, physical isolation creates an effective barrier to gene flow, thereby creating prezygotic isolation.
After allopatric speciation, prezygotic isolation is reinforced after populations engaging in this process produce low-fitness hybrids. This process occurs when two allopatric populations reunite.
These insects are typically used as model organisms when studying allopatric speciation in a lab setting. Thomas Hunt Morgan studied genetic linkage by cross-breeding these insects.

bonuses.leadin: Robert Laughlin explained a version of this effect using fractionally-charged quasiparticles. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this effect, the integer version of which was discovered in the inversion layer of a MOSFET. In this effect, the resistance takes on values equal to one over an integer, all times the von Klitzing constant.

The quantum Hall effect, like the classical Hall effect, is induced by applying one of these fields perpendicularly to a current. These fields are measured in teslas and always have both north and south poles.
This topological quantum field theory developed by Ed Witten can be used to explain the exactitude of the values in the fractional quantum Hall effect.

bonuses.leadin: The motto “Rebellion to tyrants is obedience to God” was printed on one of these objects of mammoth proportions gifted to Thomas Jefferson. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this kind of object which the citizens of Cheshire, Massachusetts created in 1802. A massive one of these objects spent two years in the White House after being gifted by Oswego, New York to Andrew Jackson.

This person once asked “how can you govern a country which has two hundred and forty-six varieties of cheese.” Less cheesy exploits of this person included leading the Free French in Africa during World War II.

A group of Somerset farmers gifted this ruler a massive cheese as a wedding gift. According to Shrabani Basu, this ruler befriended the royal servant Abdul “the Munshi” Karim after having his chicken curry.

bonuses.leadin: In a postscript, Bernard Williams admitted that when he first introduced this concept, he “expected to suggest an oxymoron.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this phenomenon Williams illustrated with a painter who makes masterpieces after abandoning his family. Another thinker used the Control Principle and a car accident to illustrate this concept.
This thinker expanded on Williams’ concept of moral luck by dividing it into types like constitutive and resultant. This thinker also wrote “What is it like to be a Bat?”

Nagel wrote that his causal form of moral luck is roughly equivalent to a problem regarding this concept, in which people have volition to make their own decisions. Hard determinists reject this concept.

bonuses.leadin: Description acceptable. The target of this event noted that the 27 seconds it took were enough to read his favorite Shakespeare sonnet aloud in the 2024 memoir Knife. For 10 points each:
parts: Identify or describe this August 2022 event carried out by Hadi Matar, which occurred during a lecture on the Chautauqua circuit.
Matar claimed to have only read “a couple pages” of this Rushdie book but agreed with the views of Ayatollah Khomeini, who issued a fatwa against Rushdie for its publication.

Rushdie represented Khomeini with this book’s villainous Khattam-Shud, who aims to silence the talkative residents of Gup. This book is set on the moon Kahani, which is divided into Gup and the silent Chup.

bonuses.leadin: This artist collaborated with Matthias Grünewald (“GRUH-nuh-vald”) on the Heller Altarpiece. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this artist who depicted a dog and lion sleeping before a studying saint in one work. Another work by this artist shows an angel brooding next to a rhombohedron.
Dürer added a large lake in his Landauer Altarpiece as an homage to Albrecht Altdorfer, an artist known for this genre of paintings that depict the natural scenery of an environment.

The central panel of Dürer’s first altarpiece, named for this city, features a scene of Mary Adoring the Child. Mary sits on a throne draped with an oriental carpet in a triptych named for this non-Ghent city by Jan van Eyck.

bonuses.leadin: The speaker cheers “Hurrah for the pumpkin pie!” as they arrive at this location “through the white and drifted snow.” For 10 points each:
parts: Name this specific location to which the speaker travels in Lydia Maria Child’s Thanksgiving poem “Over the River and Through the Wood.”

The narrator of this book lives in a tiny garret in her grandmother’s house for seven years to escape the abusive Dr. Flint. Lydia Maria Child helped publish this book, whose author used the pseudonym Linda Brent.
Harriet Jacobs’ Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl is a work in this genre. Frederick Douglass wrote a notable work in this genre, which also includes Booker T. Washington’s Up From Slavery.

bonuses.leadin: According to this teaching, a religion’s namesake prophet, who was born in 1817, is the most recent messenger aiding in the spiritual evolution of humans in a cycle split by intervals of 500 to 1,000 years. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this process described by the Báb, in which messengers called Manifestations of God like Moses, Jesus, and Buddha adapt particulars of their practice and appearance to their time.
Progressive revelation is a core tenet of this monotheistic religion originating in Iran, which believes in the unity of all religions and developed from the earlier Bábi Faith.

The founder of Baháʼí, Baháʼu'lláh, called this concept “the light of men” and said it was necessary for “the appearance of unity among men”. The Universal House of this concept in Haifa, Israel is the center of the Baháʼí faith.

bonuses.leadin: This device uses solutions of copper sulfate and zinc sulfate. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this eponymous electrochemical cell that contains copper and zinc electrodes. This cell was used in the original definition of the volt.
Electrochemical cells take advantage of reactions at the anode and this other electrode where reduction occurs. This word also lends itself to a “ray tube” used in televisions.

Lithium anode batteries can be paired with this inorganic compound to yield high-specific energy, non-rechargable batteries. This toxic non-aqueous electrolyte can be paired with aluminum trichloride.

bonuses.leadin: John Lynch described this dynasty’s colonial reforms as a “second conquest” that limited the power of local-born elites and replaced corregidores (“co-ray-hee-doors”) with intendants. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this dynasty which was forced to grant the asiento monopoly on the slave trade with its colonies to British merchants during peace negotiations at Utrecht, which also split this royal house into two distinct lines.
The installation of Philip V as the Bourbon king of Spain was a success for this French “Sun King”, Philip’s grandfather who passed away a year later after 72 years of rule.

Philip V promulgated the Nueva Planta decrees, which centralized government under Castile and abolished these legal charters that granted privileges in Valencia, Catalonia, Aragon, and the Basque Country.

bonuses.leadin: This piece’s “Intermezzo interrotto” fourth movement features a trombone glissando that is not possible on modern instruments since it was originally written for a bass trombone pitched in F. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this work, whose fourth movement also includes a quote from Franz Lehár's The Merry Widow as a parody of Shostakovich’s earlier quote of the work in his Leningrad Symphony.

This composer drew inspiration from his country’s folk music for his Concerto for Orchestra. This Hungarian composer and ethnomusicologist composed The Miraculous Mandarin and is known for his style of “night music.”
In works like Concerto for Orchestra and The Miraculous Mandarin, Bartok frequently called for this technique in his brass parts, denoted by the instruction con sordino.
